narratives.ProblemStatement: Fiction writers and AI writing systems like Autonomicon lack tools that provide structured, genre-aware literary critique at the craft level. Generic writing tools offer surface-level grammar and style checks but cannot evaluate narrative structure, character arcs, pacing, thematic coherence, or the holistic question: 'Is this story enjoyable to read?' Writers need a beta reader that is consistent, available on demand, and produces actionable diagnostic feedback grounded in genre expectations.
narratives.Goals: 1. Answer 'is this enjoyable to read?' with structured, evidence-backed diagnostic feedback. 2. Analyze prose quality, narrative structure, consistency, and pacing using specialized AI agents. 3. Work at any granularity — single chapter, groups of chapters, or full novels. 4. Serve as a quality benchmark and regression surface for Autonomicon-generated fiction. 5. Remain local-first, privacy-focused, and extensible.
narratives.UserStories: US-1: As a writer, I want to analyze a chapter and get structured feedback on prose quality so I can identify specific weaknesses. US-2: As a writer, I want to analyze a full manuscript directory and get cross-chapter narrative feedback (arcs, pacing, continuity). US-3: As a writer, I want to ask follow-up questions about the analysis so I can understand the reasoning behind specific feedback. US-4: As a writer, I want to compare two manuscripts side-by-side so I can measure quality improvement. US-5: As an Autonomicon operator, I want genre-aware analysis so critique respects the conventions of the target genre. US-6: As a writer, I want to see repetition patterns detected algorithmically so the tool catches what LLMs miss (word frequency, phrase reuse, author tics). US-7: As a writer, I want analysis to resume from where it left off if the API fails mid-run.
narratives.Requirements: FR-1: 'ghostreader init <project_name>' creates project folder with config.yaml and .ghostreader/ state directory. FR-2: 'ghostreader analyze <path>' auto-detects file vs. directory; processes .md (primary) and .epub (secondary) inputs. FR-3: 'ghostreader chat <project>' provides conversational RAG over stored analysis results. FR-4: 'ghostreader compare <path1> <path2>' produces side-by-side quality scorecard with per-dimension metrics and deltas. FR-5: 'ghostreader config' views and edits configuration (default model, genre, depth). FR-6: Ingestion node loads markdown files, detects chapters via chapter-NNN.md naming convention (sorted by filename), builds hierarchical summaries (chapter > act > global). FR-7: Epub ingestion via ebooklib + stdlib xml.etree.ElementTree for XHTML-to-text conversion. FR-8: Prose Analyst agent evaluates repetition patterns (from pre-processing), sentence rhythm and variety, show-vs-tell ratio, dialogue naturalness, vocabulary richness, and style. FR-9: Narrative Analyst agent evaluates character arcs and consistency, pacing and tension curves, theme and motif usage, structural patterns, and world-building coherence. FR-10: Consistency Checker agent detects logical inconsistencies, plot holes, timeline/continuity errors, foreshadowing effectiveness, and unresolved threads. FR-11: Synthesis Agent combines all agent outputs, generates executive summary, assigns severity ratings (strength/neutral/concern) per dimension, and produces prioritized diagnostic feedback with cited evidence. FR-12: Algorithmic repetition detection (tf-idf + fuzzy matching) runs as pre-processing during ingestion; results stored as structured data in LangGraph state and fed to Prose Analyst. FR-13: LanceDB vector store indexes manuscript chunks and analysis results for retrieval (chat command and cross-chapter context). FR-14: Analysis caching — avoid re-analyzing unchanged sections; persist vector index, analysis results, and chapter summaries under .ghostreader/. FR-15: Checkpoint-and-resume on API failure — completed chapters are saved, analysis resumes from last incomplete chapter. FR-16: Genre-aware prompt framing via --genre flag; genre modifies agent system prompts, not agent pipeline structure. FR-17: Configurable model selection via config.yaml (default) and --model flag (override); user-configured preference order. FR-18: Rich terminal output via Rich library with color-coded sections. FR-19: Full report saved as markdown at reports/manuscript_name_YYYY-MM-DD.md with inline chapter/line references. FR-20: JSON output option via --format json for scripting and Autonomicon integration. FR-21: Analysis depth control via --depth flag (quick/standard/deep) controlling agent thoroughness. FR-22: Example rewrites are opt-in via --show-rewrites flag, not included by default. NFR-1: Handle full novels (~100k words) via two-pass architecture — summary pass then per-chunk agent analysis with retrieval context. NFR-2: Local-first, privacy-focused — all processing uses user-provided API keys, no data leaves user infrastructure. NFR-3: Works at any granularity — single chapter adapts by skipping cross-chapter summary layer. NFR-4: Test coverage >= 85% overall and per-module. NFR-5: Output is diagnostic ('this passage tells instead of shows') not prescriptive ('rewrite it like this'). NFR-6: Extensible — easy to add new analysis agents or critique lenses.
narratives.SuccessMetrics: 1. Ghostreader produces actionable feedback that identifies at least 3 concrete improvement areas per chapter on standard depth. 2. Analysis of a 20-chapter manuscript completes within a reasonable time using API models. 3. Repetition detection catches word/phrase/structure patterns that LLM-only analysis misses. 4. Compare scorecard shows measurable dimension-level deltas between two manuscripts. 5. Chat command answers questions about analysis with cited evidence from the stored results. 6. Checkpoint-and-resume successfully recovers from mid-analysis API failures without re-processing completed chapters.
narratives.Architecture: LangGraph stateful workflow with four specialized agent nodes and a pre-processing step. Pipeline: Ingestion Node (load files, detect chapters, build hierarchical summaries, index into LanceDB) -> Repetition Detector (algorithmic tf-idf + fuzzy matching, outputs structured data) -> [Prose Analyst + Narrative Analyst + Consistency Checker] (parallel, each receives chunk + retrieval context + summary hierarchy + repetition data) -> Synthesis Agent (combines outputs, assigns severity ratings, produces prioritized diagnostic report). Two-pass architecture: Pass 1 builds chapter/act/global summaries stored in LangGraph shared state. Pass 2 runs each agent per-chunk with the summary hierarchy providing whole-manuscript awareness. Conditional routing: --depth flag controls agent thoroughness (quick skips deep sub-analyses). State persistence: .ghostreader/ directory stores LanceDB index, analysis results as JSON, chapter summaries. Chat command rehydrates from these artifacts for RAG retrieval. Tech stack: Python 3.12+, Typer (CLI), Rich (terminal UI), LangGraph + LangChain (openai/anthropic/ollama), LanceDB (vector store), pydantic + PyYAML (config), ebooklib + markdown (input formats).
narratives.Overview: Ghostreader is a CLI-based AI literary analysis tool that functions as an intelligent beta reader. It reads fiction manuscripts and delivers structured, genre-aware diagnostic feedback answering the question: 'Is this story enjoyable to read?' Built primarily to evaluate Autonomicon-generated fiction, it uses specialized LangGraph agents for prose analysis, narrative structure, and consistency checking, with algorithmic repetition detection for pattern-matching that LLMs miss.
